prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Your desktop companion is being prepared and will land on your screen shortly."]
1: ["Your Companion is Ready", "Right-click your pet on the desktop anytime to open controls, change settings, or hide it."]
2: ["Choose Your Path", "Pick a ready-to-go companion or create a custom pet from your photos."]
3: ["Pet Adopted Successfully!", "Look at your desktop to find your pet. Use right-click for options and interactions."]
4: ["Use clear, well-lit, front-facing photos of a single pet for the best custom rendering result."]
5: ["Authenticating your account securely. Please wait a moment."]
6: ["Bring Your Desktop to Life in 60 Seconds", "Choose or build an interactive virtual companion that stays on your screen while you work."]
7: ["Add Pet Photos"]
8: ["Quick Desktop Pet Tips", "While your pet loads: Right-click for menu, drag to move around your screen, or double-click to play."]
9: ["Save Your Pet to Your Account", "Sign in now to sync your new companion across your devices."]
